# 2012A Question 5 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

Using opioids as examples [**describe**]{.task-verb} and [**illustrate with graphs**]{.task-verb} what you understand by the terms "potency", "efficacy", "partial agonist", "competitive antagonist", and "therapeutic index".
:::

Also asked in: [2005B Question 2](/content/exams/anzca/2005/B/2/index.qmd#examiner-comments), [2018B Question 7](/content/exams/anzca/2018/B/7/index.qmd#examiner-comments), [2020B Question 11](/content/exams/anzca/2020/B/11/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Describe and illustrate**]{.task-verb} each term with a precise definition, opioid example and labelled graph. Distinguish graded from quantal responses and keep dose or concentration on the horizontal axis.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Potency: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph

### Efficacy: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph

### Partial Agonism: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph

### Competitive Antagonism: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph

### Therapeutic Index: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**46 %** of candidates passed this question.

Potency is the relative dose required for a given effect. It largely determines the dose administered. It is best illustrated with log dose – response curves. Examples of opioids drawn according to the relative potency were expected. Extra marks were given for clear descriptions about ED50, and distinguishing between potency and affinity.

Efficacy is the maximal effect able to be achieved by the drug regardless of dose. It is used to compare the drug’s ability to elicit a full or partial biological response. Bonus marks for discussing why this occurs. A partial agonist is a drug whose maximum effect is less than a full agonist, e.g. buprenorphine vs. morphine.

Competitive antagonists are drugs which compete at the same receptor to reverse the effect of an agonist, e.g. naloxone and morphine.    This can be overcome by increasing the agonist concentration. Bonus marks were awarded to those who distinguished it from non-competitive antagonism.

Therapeutic index is based on quantal dose response curves. It is the lethal dose in 50% of population divided by the effective dose in 50% of the population. This type of data is available only in animal studies. Human studies are limited and toxic dose is used instead of lethal dose, e.g. respiratory depression vs analgesia for opioids. It is not the therapeutic range. Extra marks were awarded for discussing the limitations of therapeutic index.

Common omissions were failure to discuss all five concepts or failure to use appropriately labelled graphs or opioids as examples.
:::
